analysis.reading: The thesis is named, attributed and placed correctly, and the Robinson (1976) and Gentry (1989) lineage comes from the deposit itself: #202 situates the argument 'within an existing minority scholarly tradition' and names both. What the composition does not carry is the claim the deposit's title exists to make. #202 is 'Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early': 'Early concedes the Pauline timeline and asks for an adjusted date within it. First rejects the inferential basis of the Pauline timeline.' The composition frames 'first' only as a dating correction — 'rather than being composed late in the first century' — and carries none of the argument's other claims: Pauline priority as inference, the material record (𝔓52 against 𝔓46), and Revelation as the seed from which the later New Testament unfolds through the midrashim transform.
